newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Downer to visit Europe for trade talks.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Downer to visit Europe for trade talks.

text.p: Australian Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer said on Wednesday he would meet political and business leaders in Europe from January 25 to February 7 to discuss trade and investment.

Meetings in the Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and Italy were expected to focus on further development of Australia's commercial and political relationship with the European Union, Downer said in a statement.

"I also intend to promote Australia's interest and involvement in Asian regional economic and security issues through keynote addresses to foreign policy institutes in London and in The Hague," he said.

His intinerary includes addressing the opening session of the United Nations conference on disarmament in Geneva, a private audience with Pope John Paul II in Rome, and official discussions on the Northern Ireland situation in London.
He will visit the Netherlands from January 27 to 28, discussing Australia's relationship with the European Union, including talks with heads of the international criminal and justice courts.
On January 29 Downer will discuss political and commercial issues in Brussels with the European Commission, including talks on the EU-Australia Framework agreement.

The visit to Switzerland, from January 30 to February 3, while including an address to the U.N., will also enable Downer to table the report of the Canberra Commission on the elimination of nuclear weapons. He said he would also reaffirm Australia's commitment to a worldwide ban on land mines.

Downer will meet the new U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan and other representatives in Switzerland and attend the annual meeting of the World Economic Forum in Davos to discuss security in Asia and international trade.
In London, from February 4 to 5, Downer will discuss British policy towards Northern Ireland with officials and other bilateral issues with key political leaders.

The focal point of his visit to Italy, from February 6 to 7, will be the revitalising of Australia's political and commercial relationship with Italy, including private talks with the Pope John Paul II.
